extracted.intended_audience: state and tribal title IV-E agencies, child welfare administrators, tribes, legal service providers, and program fiscal staff
extracted.subtask_short: claiming IV-E FFP for legal representation
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and allowable-claim rules for Title IV-E agencies to claim Federal financial participation (FFP) for administrative costs of legal representation in foster care and related civil proceedings, including tribal representation and independent representation. Covers definitions, documentation, scope, limits, and reporting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFP rate for allowable administrative costs
rubrics_metrics.description: A title IV-E agency may claim FFP at the rate of 50 percent for allowable title IV-E foster care administrative costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 50% FFP rate applies to allowable administrative costs described in 45 CFR 1356.60, including the legal representation costs enumerated in paragraph (c)(4). Title IV-E agencies determine which administrative costs are necessary to administer their title IV-E foster care program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs related to legal representation (§1356.60(c)(2)(xi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (c)(2)(xi) provides that allowable administrative costs include 'Costs related to legal representation described in paragraph (c)(4) of this section.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cross-reference means the specific legal representation activities listed in paragraph (c)(4) are claimable as allowable administrative costs under (c)(2)(xi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable costs — attorney representing title IV-E agency or other public agency/tribe (§1356.60(c)(4)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal representation in foster care proceedings provided by an attorney representing the title IV-E agency or any other public agency (including an Indian tribe) which has an agreement in effect under which the other agency has placement and care responsibility of a title IV-E eligible child pursuant to 472(a)(2)(B)(ii) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To claim these costs, the 'other public agency' (including a tribe) must have an agreement under which it takes placement and care responsibility of title IV-E eligible children and is operating all or part of the title IV-E program on behalf of the title IV-E agency. See CWPM 8.1G for more detail. This regulatory text clarifies inclusion of tribes but does not change substantive meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable costs — independent legal representation (§1356.60(c)(4)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent legal representation provided by an attorney representing a child in title IV-E foster care, a child who is a candidate for title IV-E foster care, the child's parent(s), the child's relative caregiver(s), and the child's Indian custodian(s) in foster care and other civil legal proceedings as necessary to carry out the requirements in the agency's title IV-E foster care plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent legal representation in civil proceedings explicitly includes 'facilitating, arranging, brokering, advocating, or otherwise linking clients with providers and services as identified in the child's case plan pursuant to sections 422, 471(a)(16), and 475 of the Act.' Title IV-E agencies may claim these costs when they are necessary to carry out plan requirements. The rule leaves agencies discretion to decide what 'independent' means, subject to minimum expectations described elsewhere in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable costs — tribal representation when tribe participates/intervenes (§1356.60(c)(4)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal representation provided by an attorney representing an Indian child's tribe (as defined by 25 U.S.C.1903(5)), or representation of an Indian child's tribe provided by a non-attorney, when the child's tribe participates or intervenes in any state court proceeding for the foster care placement or termination of parental rights of an Indian child who is in title IV-E foster care or an Indian child who is a candidate for title IV-E foster care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits title IV-E agencies to claim administrative costs for tribal representation in state foster care proceedings (including TPR proceedings) when the tribe participates or intervenes. The preamble explains how tribal attorney input can be necessary to establish cultural/social standards for reasonable-efforts determinations and permanency planning under ICWA and title IV-E requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/expectations for 'independent' legal representation
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the final rule, the term 'independent' conveys that representation is not subject to control or influence by other parties, interested persons, nor the title IV-E agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble suggests (but does not require) minimum expectations agencies should consider when deciding what 'independent' means, e.g., ensuring no concurrent conflicts of interest, no interference with the lawyer's professional judgment or relationship with the client, and (suggestively) that attorneys not accept compensation from someone other than the client unless the client gives informed consent. The rule does not regulate the practice of law or try to define attorney ethical duties; agencies lack authority to regulate attorneys' practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of 'candidate for title IV-E foster care'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'candidate' for title IV-E foster care must be documented by the title IV-E agency through one of the acceptable methods identified in the Child Welfare Policy Manual (e.g., a case plan). A child is not a candidate merely because described as 'at risk' without formal agency involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IV-E agencies must follow CWPM 8.1D methods to document candidacy; the agency must have either pursued removal or made reasonable efforts to prevent removal and record the candidacy per acceptable methods. Agencies should contact CB regional offices for guidance on documentation and claiming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support professionals and related activities may be claimed when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IV-E agencies may claim administrative costs for activities necessary to support an attorney providing independent legal representation (e.g., paralegals, investigators, peer partners, social workers), but the regulatory text does not list all possible activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACF confirms these support activities are claimable to the extent necessary but declined to exhaustively list them in regulation. Agencies may contact CB regional offices for assistance on specific allowable activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope includes foster care and other civil legal proceedings necessary to carry out the foster care plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule covers legal representation in foster care proceedings and in 'other civil legal proceedings' when those proceedings are necessary to carry out requirements in the title IV-E agency's foster care plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include facilitating access to services identified in case plans, referrals, and other civil matters that affect reunification or permanency. The preamble rejected limiting the text to only 'civil' (i.e., it covers both foster care legal proceedings and other civil legal proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions: agency caseworkers' hearing-preparation costs and out-of-scope matters
rubrics_metrics.description: New paragraph (c)(4) does not include the costs of agency caseworkers preparing for and participating in hearings (those remain within paragraph (c)(2)(ii)). Also, requests to require training, prescribe contracting/oversight models, or change cost-allocation law were deemed out of scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IV-E agencies should continue to rely on (c)(2)(ii) for caseworker-related preparation costs. Other matters (training standards, contracting models, cost-allocation rules) are governed elsewhere (e.g., 45 CFR parts 75 and 95) or are optional and outside this rule's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may claim FFP (eligibility to claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only state and tribal title IV-E agencies with an approved title IV-E foster care plan may claim FFP for the administrative costs described; title IV-E agencies may contract with public and private entities to perform administrative functions, but other public agencies, organizations, or individuals may not claim title IV-E funds directly from the Federal Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IV-E agencies have discretion whether to claim FFP for allowable legal representation costs; the rule does not compel agencies to provide legal representation or to claim the funds. Contracts and agreements should comply with CWPM and applicable statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal eligibility and agreements under 472(a)(2)(B)(ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: A title IV-E agency may claim FFP for allowable costs of an attorney providing legal representation of an Indian tribe in foster care proceedings only if the Indian tribe has an agreement under which it takes placement and care responsibility of title IV-E eligible children and is operating all or part of the title IV-E program on behalf of the title IV-E agency (section 472(a)(2)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACF declined to revise the regulation further but points to CWPM 8.1G for more information on agreements; this clarifies when tribes are treated as 'other public agency' for purposes of (c)(4)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information sharing and minimum necessary reporting for claims/audits
rubrics_metrics.description: A title IV-E agency should, at a minimum, ensure a legal service provider shares information necessary for the agency to comply with Federal program requirements and requirements for audits, data, and financial reporting as determined necessary by the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may include information required for Form CB-496 (Title IV-E Programs Quarterly Financial Report) and other audit/reporting needs. Agencies must balance reporting needs with protecting independence of representation and avoiding undue influence; providers expressed concern about overbroad information requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent representation may include non-litigation activities identified in case plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent legal representation in civil proceedings includes facilitating, arranging, brokering, advocating, or otherwise linking clients with providers and services as identified in the child's case plan pursuant to sections 422, 471(a)(16), and 475 of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affirms that non-court advocacy and service linkage done by attorneys on behalf of clients as part of case plan requirements can be claimed as allowable administrative costs when necessary to carry out the agency's title IV-E foster care plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial reporting and estimating practices referenced in preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: The preamble provides methodology and estimates for Federal and non-Federal costs, national average claims per child, and accounting statements over a ten-year horizon; these are analytical details to characterize budgetary impacts of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These estimates illustrate expected fiscal effects and are not additional legal requirements for claiming. Agencies should follow statutory and regulatory claiming rules and consult CB regional offices for allowable cost estimation and claiming procedures.
